deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is preparing his Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' in Dix exposés, 1968. On the previous page he recalls Manin's construction of the Gauss–Manin connection, which is algebraic but computational. He then states (3.5 (i)) that the Cartan homotopy formula d i_ξ + i_ξ d = θ_ξ gives a simple direct construction. If f: X → S and a derivation ξ of O_S lifts locally to a derivation ξ̄ of O_X, the action of (ξ̄, ξ) on f_*(Ω•_{X/S}) is independent of the lift up to homotopy. Hence the derivations of S act on the R^i f_*(Ω•_{X/S}), and when S is smooth over T this gives an integrable T-connection.

This page, (ii): by a technically refined version of the same idea (deferred to an appendix), suppose f is smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the complex Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}) carries a canonical 'absolute' connection in the sense of derived categories. Here 'absolute' means relative to the absolute base, with no smoothness hypothesis on S. The natural derived-category reading is a 1-stratification: an isomorphism p_1^* K ≅ p_2^* K in D(P^1_S), where P^1_S is the first-order neighbourhood of the diagonal of S.

He stresses that this does not automatically put connections on the individual cohomology sheaves R^i f_*. Taking H^i does not commute with the non-flat pullbacks p_1^*, p_2^*. It does hold when S has characteristic 0 and f is proper and smooth. Then the R^i f_* are locally free (Hodge–de Rham degeneration), their formation commutes with base change, and the derived connection descends to each R^i f_*. In characteristic p he hints that things fail, apparently even in the smooth affine case; that sentence is illegible. He adds that for f proper and smooth, compatibility with the transcendental Gauss–Manin connection (R^i f^an_* C ⊗ O_S) is trivial.

Remark (continued on the next page): one might hope these canonical connections come from canonical stratifications, i.e. infinite-order descent data, crystals on the infinitesimal site. That would give an a priori explanation of the invariance in Washnitzer–Monsky cohomology. This is true in characteristic 0 but false in characteristic p, e.g. for families of elliptic curves. The reason, in modern terms, is that the Gauss–Manin connection has nonzero p-curvature, measured by the Hasse invariant. This motivates replacing the infinitesimal site by the crystalline site.
errors: Read literally, the machine transcription's hypothesis 'lisse propre et quasi-proj.' would be odd; the manuscript most likely says 'lisse, quasi-compact et quasi-séparé', which is the natural hypothesis for Rf_* to behave well.

Characteristic 0 is not really needed for R^i f_* to be locally free and commute with base change; what is needed is Hodge–de Rham degeneration with locally free terms. The note is correct as a sufficient condition.
The characteristic-p clause is too fragmentary to check; no definite error can be identified.

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection constructed via the Cartan homotopy formula and lifting derivations
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Canonical 'absolute' connection on the complex Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}) in the derived category, over an arbitrary base S, as an isomorphism of the two pullbacks to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: derived Gauss–Manin connection / derived 1-stratification (D-module or crystal structure on the pushforward complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals), Berthelot, Illusie; later derived de Rham work
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Crystals (1968); the derived-category formulation over a non-smooth base is not clearly stated there

ideas.what: Descent of the derived connection to the individual R^i f_* requires base-change compatibility (true for proper smooth f in characteristic 0)
ideas.modern_name: base change and Hodge–de Rham degeneration

ideas.what: The Gauss–Manin connection is a stratification (crystal on the infinitesimal site) in characteristic 0 but not in characteristic p, with elliptic curves as counterexample
ideas.modern_name: nonzero p-curvature of Gauss–Manin (Hasse invariant); need for the crystalline site
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes

missed.claim: An early explicit formulation of the Gauss–Manin connection as a canonical absolute connection on the complex Rf_*(Ω•) in the derived category, over an arbitrary (non-smooth) base. It comes with the explicit caveat that it does not automatically descend to the cohomology sheaves. The construction itself is relegated to an appendix not on this page.
missed.quote: les Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}) est muni d'une connexion absolue canonique [au sens des catégories dérivées]. Cela ne signifie pas tout à fait que les R^if_*(Ω•_{X/S}) sont munis individuellement de connexions absolues
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates derived-category and derived-de-Rham treatments of Gauss–Manin over singular bases. It is of historical interest; the idea is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Essentially the material of Grothendieck's published 'Crystals' lectures: the Gauss–Manin connection, char 0 vs char p, and the elliptic-curve counterexample. The derived-category 'absolute connection' over an arbitrary base is a mildly interesting early formulation, but its substance is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'si f est lisse propre[?] et quasi-proj.' most likely reads 'si f est lisse, qu.-compact et qu.-séparé' ('quasi-compact et quasi-séparé').
'les Rf_*(...) est muni' should read 'le Rf_*(...) est muni' (singular complex).
'[au sens des catégories dérivées]': the manuscript uses parentheses/brackets as '(au sens des catégories dérivées)'.
'eux-mêmes commutent[?] : à l'extension[?] de la base' is probably 'commutent à l'extension de la base'.
The characteristic-p clause 'dans le cas lisse affine aussi[?] les cis[?] ...' is uncertain; possibly 'même dans le cas lisse affine on a des ...'.
